rows.etymology: 46. PKT *-kʰud̤i ‘some, few, little’, Sad. kəṭik ‘little’ — Proto-Kherwarian *kaʈiʄ ‘a little (adverb)’, As. kati ‘a little’, Mu. huɖi ‘few’, Ju. kuʈiʄ ‘a little, some, few’, Sant. (Singhbhum) kəʈiʔc ‘few’; Mu. (Karimpur) hudiŋ ‘some’, Ju. (Keonjhar) kitti, kiti ‘some’. See Pinnow (103) with additional Munda forms; however, his MK equations are not convincing. Since I assume that the three last quoted forms and As. are the closest to the ‘original’ lemma, cf. the following — Tˈin kat and kɛ́ːt both ‘some’, Pacoh kɛt ‘small, little in size, age, status’, Kui kɛːt ‘small, little’ and Bru kɛːt ‘small’, perhaps also Pnar katu katni ‘some’.
